findings.asked: Form and solve two simultaneous equations from a context.
findings.wentWrong: Many set up both equations; some then added instead of subtracting; trial and error scored nothing.
findings.rule: Same signs subtract, different signs add.

findings.asked: A problem solved with simultaneous equations.
findings.wentWrong: Very well solved; a minority used trial and improvement and earned nothing beyond the setup.

findings.asked: Solve a pair where both equations must be multiplied.
findings.wentWrong: The first two marks for matching coefficients were widely earned; then some added one side and subtracted the other, and some stalled at 19x = 152.
findings.rule: Do the same operation to the whole of both equations.

findings.asked: Construct and solve simultaneous equations needing both equations scaled.
findings.wentWrong: Setting up was fine; scaling both equations and finding a multiple of 19 defeated some; over half completed it.
findings.rule: Scale to the lowest common multiple of one variable's coefficients.

findings.wentWrong: Those who knew the method earned marks despite slips; trial and error again scored zero.
findings.rule: Method marks come from the algebra, not the answer.

findings.wentWrong: The majority scored full marks; under a tenth could not set up the equations.
findings.rule: Define the two unknowns, then translate each sentence.

ruleToRemember: Label the equations, scale to match a coefficient, apply the same add or subtract to both sides in full, substitute back and check in the other equation - a guessed answer earns nothing.
aStarSignal: Both equations scaled, elimination done cleanly, and the solution checked, all without a calculator.
